text:
maria: quick heads-up — I opened a PR that tweaks the Go SDK retry defaults and adds a small streaming resume tweak. asking for a quick sanity check before we roll to beta.

sam: link?

maria: https://github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/pull/412 :arrow_up_small: main changes: default max_retries=5 (was 3), full jitter backoff, and a 2s grace window for stream resume tokens to avoid spurious idempotency failures.

cheng: pinged. curious why 5 vs 4? cost tradeoffs?

maria: 4 was borderline on a few flaky infra incidents. we measured successful request recovery increasing ~6% going from 3->5 for short 429 bursts. cost bump is tiny for our customers due to early-success short-circuits.

ryan: can you paste the backoff math you used? want to match in Rust SDK and node SDK.

maria: sure — using full jitter per AWS paper. algorithm: sleep = random_between(0, base * 2^attempt) capped at max_backoff. base=200ms, max_backoff=10s. pseudo: ```go // attempt starts at 0 delay := rand.Int63n(base * (1 << attempt)) if delay > maxBackoff { delay = maxBackoff } time.Sleep(time.Duration(delay) * time.Millisecond) ```

eden: couple questions: (1) how do we treat 429 with Retry-After? (2) idempotency for POSTs with streaming?

maria: good q. (1) If server returns Retry-After (seconds or HTTP-date) we respect it and override computed backoff (but still jitter around it: we use rand_between(0, retry_after) to avoid stampede). (2) For streaming upload/generate endpoints, we require Idempotency-Key for any client retry that could re-run user-supplied prompts that cause side effects. Without the key we only retry safe cases (idempotent GET/HEAD) or we surface a non-retriable error.

sam: for streaming resume, what's the 2s grace window?

maria: when the client reconnects and presents a resume token, we accept tokens up to 2s older than server's last seen position to account for clock skew and network jitter. if token is older than that we reject and suggest re-starting stream or using Idempotency-Key to replay.

ryan: in Rust SDK PR I have a slightly different approach — we exponential backoff but multiply Retry-After by 0.8 to be conservative. any preference?

maria: I'd prefer following server-specified Retry-After literally so client doesn't under-wait and cause more 429s; but adding small randomness is fine. matching behaviour across SDKs is higher priority.

cheng: code review notes: please add unit tests for parsing HTTP-date in Retry-After (Edge case: Apache returns GMT spelled different), and add an integration test where server returns 503 then 200 to check attempt counting.

maria: added tests in the PR: RetryAfter parser + 503->200 scenario. also added telemetry tag retry.policy=full-jitter-go.

retry-bot: CI: go-sdk/pr-412 — build passed, tests passed, coverage +0.3%.

eden: any breaking change for customers?

maria: behavioral change is only defaults; explicit configs are unchanged. we'll call out in changelog and the SDK release notes. also adding migration snippet in docs: 
```
client := redwood.NewClient(redwood.Config{MaxRetries: 3}) // restore old behavior
```

sam: can we coordinate a short announcement on the SDK changelog + migration notes in docs before release? I can take that.

maria: thanks — assigning to @sam for the write-up. I'll queue a follow-up to sync with docs. :thumbsup:

ryan: I'll align Rust and Node PRs to use same retry semantics. will ping back if anything diverges.

maria: perfect. if anyone sees any odd streaming behavior in nightly, flag it here and we'll revert the default until we validate. thanks all. :raised_hands:
